_about: Which firmware supports each feature the Protocol Pro design relies on. Every cell is backed by the firmware's own documentation or source at the linked page. Support levels: yes, partial (works with changes or a custom build, or only in part), no, unconfirmed. Cells rate what the firmware can do; the board row says whether it runs on the Cube Orange+ at all.

ardupilot.how: Official CubeOrangePlus hwdef (STM32H757, with the IOMCU on USART6) built for every release.

px4.how: Official target cubepilot_cubeorangeplus, shipped since v1.14 and not interchangeable with Cube Orange firmware.

betaflight.how: No Cube Orange or Cube Orange+ board config exists; 2026.6 only adds a generic STM32H757 MCU, and there is no driver for the IOMCU that drives the 8 MAIN outputs, so a custom board config would be needed.

features.feature: MAVLink 2 telemetry, parameters, missions and signing

ardupilot.how: SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 2 at SERIALn_BAUD = 57 with the full parameter and mission protocols, and MAVLink 2 signing on MAVLink 2 ports.

px4.how: MAVLink 2 to the ground station with parameters and missions on TELEM1, but message signing exists only in the main branch, not in v1.16.2 or v1.17.0.

betaflight.how: The MAVLink serial function streams telemetry and 2026.6 adds mission upload, but there is no MAVLink parameter protocol and no signing.

features.feature: ROS 2 over micro XRCE-DDS to the Jetson

ardupilot.how: AP_DDS is left out of the standard Cube Orange+ build, so it needs a custom build with DDS, then SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 45 and DDS_ENABLE = 1.

px4.how: The uXRCE-DDS client is in the default Cube Orange+ build; free TELEM2 with MAV_1_CONFIG = 0 and set UXRCE_DDS_CFG = TELEM2.

betaflight.how: No DDS or XRCE client exists in the source tree.

features.feature: Guided or offboard control from the companion over MAVLink

ardupilot.how: Guided mode accepts SET_POSITION_TARGET_LOCAL_NED, SET_POSITION_TARGET_GLOBAL_INT and SET_ATTITUDE_TARGET from the companion on USB (SERIAL0).

px4.how: Offboard mode accepts the same setpoint messages and needs a stream of at least 2 Hz.

betaflight.how: There is no guided or offboard mode; MAVLink input only accepts RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE and RADIO_STATUS, and USB speaks MSP.

features.feature: DroneCAN GPS, compass, barometer, LED and buzzer (Here4)

ardupilot.how: CAN_P1_DRIVER = 1, CAN_D1_PROTOCOL = 1 and GPS1_TYPE = 9; every Here4 sensor and the LED and buzzer are found automatically.

px4.how: UAVCAN_ENABLE = 2 with GPS and compass on by default and UAVCAN_SUB_BARO = 1 for the barometer, but the docs name only the Here3, not the Here4.

betaflight.how: 2026.6 adds initial DroneCAN with GNSS, compass and ESCs but no barometer, LED or buzzer; 2025.12 has no CAN at all.

features.feature: RTK corrections from GPS_RTCM_DATA forwarded to the CAN GPS

ardupilot.how: GPS_RTCM_DATA is reassembled and sent on as uavcan.equipment.gnss.RTCMStream, to every GPS by default (GPS_INJECT_TO = 127).

px4.how: QGroundControl sends GPS_RTCM_DATA and UAVCAN_PUB_RTCM = 1 publishes it on the CAN bus.

betaflight.how: No GPS_RTCM_DATA handler, and the DroneCAN GNSS code only reads fixes.

features.feature: SIYI A8 mini gimbal over its serial protocol

ardupilot.how: Native driver: MNT1_TYPE = 8, SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 8 at SERIALn_BAUD = 115; the A8 is listed as supported.

px4.how: No SIYI driver; it works only if the A8 mini speaks MAVLink Gimbal Protocol v2 (MNT_MODE_IN = 4, MNT_MODE_OUT = 2), which SIYI does not document, or through the companion.

betaflight.how: The only serial gimbal support is a head tracker protocol for FPV gimbals, not SIYI's.

features.feature: ExpressLRS over CRSF at 420000 baud with telemetry

ardupilot.how: SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 23 with RC_OPTIONS bit 13 for the 420k ELRS rate; CRSF telemetry is built in.

px4.how: The crsf_rc driver (RC_CRSF_PRT_CFG) is not in the Cube Orange+ build, so a custom build that enables it is needed.

betaflight.how: serialrx_provider = CRSF, the default, with CRSF telemetry.

features.feature: Benewake TFmini-S rangefinder on I2C at 0x10

px4.how: The tfmini driver supports the TFmini-S only over UART (SENS_TFMINI_CFG); the only Benewake I2C driver is tf02pro, and whether it works with a TFmini-S is unconfirmed.

betaflight.how: rangefinder_hardware = TFMINI is serial only, so the sensor would have to move to a UART.

features.feature: DShot300 to BLHeli_S ESCs on the AUX outputs

ardupilot.how: MOT_PWM_TYPE = 5; AUX outputs support DShot, and bidirectional DShot is listed for BLHeli32 and AM32 ESCs only.

px4.how: DShot works only on FMU outputs, which on the Cube are the AUX pins: select DShot300 for them in Actuator Configuration.

betaflight.how: motor_pwm_protocol = DSHOT300, and dshot_bidir = ON for RPM filtering on Bluejay or JESC firmware (given a custom board config for the AUX timers).

features.feature: ADS-B receiver built into the carrier board

ardupilot.how: The Cube Orange+ defaults already set ADSB_TYPE = 1 and SERIAL5_PROTOCOL = 1 at 57600 baud; AVD_ENABLE = 1 turns on avoidance.

px4.how: The receiver is configured automatically in default firmware, and NAV_TRAFF_AVOID chooses warn, return or land.

betaflight.how: No ADS-B or traffic avoidance support, and ADSB_VEHICLE is not handled.

features.feature: Missions, geofence, return to launch and terrain following

ardupilot.how: Auto missions, fence and RTL are standard, and terrain following uses the terrain database (TERRAIN_ENABLE = 1) or a rangefinder (WP_RFND_USE = 1).

px4.how: Missions, geofences and Return mode are standard, but terrain following is not available in missions, only in Position and Altitude modes (MPC_ALT_MODE = 1).

betaflight.how: GPS Rescue and position hold are standard; the 2026.6 waypoint autopilot is experimental and tested only in simulation, and there is no terrain following.

features.feature: Analog power module (PM02 V3) on POWER1

px4.how: BAT1_N_CELLS, then calibrate BAT1_V_DIV and BAT1_A_PER_V in QGroundControl, since the board defaults do not match a PM02.

betaflight.how: battery_meter = ADC with vbat_scale and ibata_scale (pins from the missing board config).

ardupilot.how: An angle P loop feeds a rate PID loop at SCHED_LOOP_RATE, 400 Hz by default for Copter.

px4.how: A quaternion attitude P loop feeds a rate PID loop at IMU_GYRO_RATEMAX, 400 Hz by default and up to 2000 Hz.

betaflight.how: The PID loop runs on every gyro sample by default (pid_process_denom = 1), typically 4 to 8 kHz, which is why it feels so sharp in manual flight.

ardupilot.how: Flat named parameters (BATT_MONITOR, SERIALn_PROTOCOL) in Mission Planner or QGroundControl; this repo generates them in protocol_pro.param.

px4.how: Named parameters through QGroundControl setup screens, with optional modules chosen at build time in the board's Kconfig.

betaflight.how: CLI set commands or the Configurator app, with optional features chosen when the firmware is built in the cloud.

notes: Checked on 2026-10-08. PX4 v1.17.0 (May 2026) is the latest stable; its Cube Orange+ build enables the same drivers as v1.16.2 for every row here, still without crsf_rc or message signing.
Betaflight 2025.12 has no CAN, no MAVLink missions and no waypoint mode; 2026.6 adds all three in early form, and the waypoint autopilot is only compiled with the USE_FLIGHT_PLAN build option.

Every Betaflight cell describes what the firmware can do. On this exact drone none of it works until someone writes a Cube Orange+ board config (IMUs, timers, ADC pins), and the 8 MAIN outputs behind the IOMCU cannot be used at all.
INAV, Betaflight's sibling with GPS navigation, adds position hold, return to home and waypoint missions; its CAN, Cube and SIYI support was not checked.

Least certain cells: PX4 with the SIYI A8 mini (no official word on MAVLink gimbal v2), PX4 with a TFmini-S on I2C, PX4 naming the Here4, and Betaflight's brand new DroneCAN and autopilot, which the release notes call initial and simulation only.
